Definition: from a compound of G1909 and G461; a straightening up again, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (reformation):-- correction.
BiblicalUsage: Epanorthosis is correction — a straightening up again — and it appears once, in Paul's claim that Scripture is profitable for it. The word pictures something bent being set straight, not punished for being bent.
TheologicalSignificance: Correction is one of Scripture's kindest gifts, I believe: God does not leave us crooked, He straightens us by His word.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
